title: Taking solos in Buddy Petit's day and on records
summary: He says solos were rare in early bands, only breaks for banjo, piano and others, and he did not believe in them.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: the show. You were playing solos in those days, huh? Yeah, we played plenty. Well, with bands like Buddy Petit's band, did you take any solos?

Well, them solos weren't much in that time. We didn't take solos. You know, on the solos it took itself, it was on the music, the coffers, you know. But this solo was by yourself. It didn't do that. This man would get tired of so many bars, he would play, he'd get tired, well, to keep his lip from swelling or something, well, he'd pull down, take a chance, but the time he'd come up, you'd felt that way, you'd take down, take a chance. And then, you know, the solo, and then, well, it was on the music. But all that solo part, that stuff come out, that's where other men get ideas on you, to know what you're doing. That's all that was for.
I know on the records you made, you took a lot of solos.

Well, they asked for solos on them records, too, on them records, a certain part of it. But I never believed in solos that way. But how we used to do it a long time ago, when they'd turn it over to me, the point of thing you say, like me, and the drums would get on low and pedal, and they'll get to our bass and piano. See, when we had that, you understand? Well, that was the only solo that we would have to take. Well, after we had a special number we'd play, take and let the banjo or guitar or piano do so much on it, and we'd give them a break in it and do so much, give them a break and do so much and take off. Yeah, there's many, many, many musicians, man. I can't call the name of it. All of the Bob Pickett and all that old bunch up there, man. That's all old time musicians. K-2, man. K-2, oh man, I can't call the name of it. What did Bob Pickett call it? Bob was a bass. I was a bass. He played the bass player. He played the bass player. I never heard of him. He played the bass player. Who did he work with? Well, a different band. He played the bass player. He played the bass player. I never heard of him. He played the bass player. Who did he work with? Well, a different band. See, that was a whole lot around there. They had a band up there too. See, it was a, in them time it was, it was a big, it was a big, it was a big, it was a tough one. like the bands on the other side of Clown Street, where you see that band, we'd be friends and all, but you know, like a distant friend. They didn't want much with the bands on this side. You know what I mean? Well out there had a couple of men in there they liked, right there, to really use them. But they were never frightened or nothing like that, but you know, just a distant friend.
